etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English vewe, from Anglo-Norman vewe, from Old French veue f (French vue f), feminine past participle of veoir (“to see”) (French voir). Cognate with Italian vedere, as well as Portuguese and Spanish ver. Doublet of veduta and vista.

definitions.definition: The act of seeing or looking at something.

quote.citation: 1671, John Milton, “The Fourth Book”, in Paradise Regain’d. A Poem. In IV Books. To which is Added, Samson Agonistes, London:  […]  J[ohn] M[acock] for John Starkey […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Thenceforth I thought thee worth my nearer view.
Objects near our view are apt to be thought greater than those of a larger size are more remote.

quote.citation: 1959, Georgette Heyer, chapter 1, in The Unknown Ajax:
quote.text: But Richmond  […]  appeared to lose himself in his own reflections. Some pickled crab, which he had not touched, had been removed with a damson pie; and his sister saw, peeping around the massive silver epergne that almost obscured him from her view, that he had eaten no more than a spoonful of that either.

quote.citation: 1697, Virgil, “(please specify the book number)”, in John Dryden, transl., The Works of Virgil: Containing His Pastorals, Georgics, and Æneis. […], London:  […]  Jacob Tonson, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: The walls of Pluto's palace are in view.

definitions.definition: Something to look at, such as scenery.

quote.citation: 1799, Thomas Campbell, The Pleasures of Hope:
quote.text: 'Tis distance lends enchantment to the view.

quote.citation: 1938, Norman Lindsay, Age of Consent, 1st Australian edition, Sydney, N.S.W.: Ure Smith, published 1962, →OCLC, page 20:
quote.text: "Well, there don't seem to be any what you might call views about here," he agreed.  […]  "I've been through the Willawee Ranges forty miles west of here, and I can guarantee the views there."

definitions.definition: (Internet) An individual viewing of a web page or a video etc. by a user.

quote.text: [Graces] which, by the splendor of her view / Dazzled, before we never knew.

definitions.definition: A picture, drawn or painted; a sketch.

quote.citation: c. 1602, William Shakespeare, “The Tragedie of Troylus and Cressida”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act V, scene v]:
quote.text: I have with exact view perused thee, Hector.

definitions.definition: A way of understanding something, an opinion, a theory.

quote.citation: 1689 (indicated as 1690), [John Locke], chapter 2, in An Essay Concerning Humane Understanding. […], London:  […]  Eliz[abeth] Holt, for Thomas Basset, […], →OCLC, book I, page 21:
quote.text: to give a right view of this mistaken part of liberty

quote.citation: 2019 May 30, Karen Weintraub, “Crispr gene-editing will change the way Americans eat – here's what's coming”, in The Guardian‎[1]:
quote.text: There hasn’t been much polling data on consumer views of gene-edited foods, because they are still so new.

quote.citation: a. 1705, John Locke, “Of the Conduct of the Understanding”, in Posthumous Works of Mr. John Locke: […], London:  […]  A[wnsham] and J[ohn] Churchill, […], published 1706, →OCLC:
quote.text: No man ever sets himself about anything but upon some view or other which serves him for a reason for what he does

quote.citation: 1903, Henry Kelsall Aspinall, Birkenhead and Its Surroundings, page 116:
quote.text: With this view, they made a Guy Faux, or dummy figure of a boy, dressed in coat and cap; such as might in a poor light be mistaken for a living figure.

definitions.definition: An opinion, judgement, imagination, idea or belief.
(computing, databases) A virtual or logical table composed of the result set of a query in relational databases.
(computing, programming) The part of a computer program which is visible to the user and can be interacted with
A wake. (Can we add an example for this sense?)

quote.citation: 2013 June 14, Jonathan Freedland, “Obama's once hip brand is now tainted”, in The Guardian Weekly, volume 189, number 1, page 18:
quote.text: Where we once sent love letters in a sealed envelope, or stuck photographs of our children in a family album, now such private material is despatched to servers and clouds operated by people we don't know and will never meet. Perhaps we assume that our name, address and search preferences will be viewed by some unseen pair of corporate eyes, probably not human, and don't mind that much.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To regard in a stated way.
